ak_lost_world_middle_earth.blurb: This is a talus boulderfield in Archangel Valley at Hatcher Pass, sitting just south of the Diamond South talus and short of Sydney Creek Bowl. There are seventeen problems, all bouldering, on granite. The spread is wide: a good number of easy problems from V0 to V2, a middle group around V3 to V5, and a pair of tough lines at V8, so both newer and strong boulderers have something. Locals have split on its name, calling it either Lost World or Middle Earth. Expect a typical alpine boulderfield, with a creek to cross on the way in.

co_stash_the.blurb: The Stash is a small bouldering sector within Hartman Rocks, the granite recreation area a few miles outside Gunnison. There are nineteen problems, and the range is broad: a few easy warm-ups at the bottom, a solid middle in the V3 to V5 band, and a short tail of harder problems reaching V7. That makes it useful for mixed groups where one person wants easy laps and another wants something to project. Hartman as a whole offers sound granite in most places, though some patches are crumbly, so test holds before trusting them.

co_big_wild_boulder.blurb: Big Wild Boulder is the largest and northernmost block in a small cluster in the Wild Rock area, high on Independence Pass between Aspen and Twin Lakes. It stands among trees, so it stays shaded through the day. There are twelve climbs: eight boulder problems from VB to V2, plus four hard bolted lines in the 5.12 to 5.13 range that feel like roped bouldering, with powerful moves from the ground up. Bring pads for the low problems and quickdraws for the sport lines.

co_bach_block_the.blurb: The Bach Block is a small sport-climbing sector at The Bank, one of the busiest parts of Shelf Road outside Canon City, where the rock is vertical limestone. There are twelve bolted routes, from about 5.7 to 5.10, and half of them fall in the 5.10 grades, so it suits climbers working through the moderate range. Three of its lines are favourites with other visitors. Because the sector sits in a popular zone, expect company on pleasant weekends.

co_waterfall_boulder.blurb: One boulder in the Wolf Creek Pass bouldering zone near South Fork, in the high country where late summer is the cool-season pick. There are a dozen problems, running from an easy warm-up through a solid middle band of V4 to V5, a trio around V7, and a few much harder lines reaching double-digit V grades. Quality varies: several problems are rated well while a couple are weak, so it works best as one stop in a larger day among the neighbouring boulders along the highway rather than a destination by itself.

co_keystone_cave_boulder.blurb: A single boulder with a cave feature, filed as one sector of the Sailing Hawks bouldering zone at the edge of Durango. There are ten problems, nearly all bouldering plus one trad line. The spread is wide: a few easy problems around V1 to V4, a cluster near V5, and several hard ones from V7 to V8, with the one roped route sitting at 5.12. Trails around the zone are well worn, which keeps navigation simple, and the larger Sailing Hawks area is regarded as one of the better places to boulder in town.

ma_gully_boulders.blurb: A pair of rounded granite boulders in the Stone Tower section of Lynn Woods, about 150 feet apart and reached by heading up a washed-out gully beside the trail. There are fourteen bouldering problems, running from an easy V1 slab through a good run of V3 to V6, with a couple of hard lines up to V8. Landings call for care, since the slab problems in particular want pads. It is a quiet side trip within the busiest, boulder-dense part of the woods, where the hike between boulders is generally short.

mt_amphitheater_area.blurb: A winter cliff in Hyalite Canyon above Bozeman, with water ice and a dense cluster of dry-tooling and mixed lines. Of the 19 climbs, most are mixed, running from around M4 up to M11, and the ice is mainly WI3 and WI4. It is one of the easier ice venues in the canyon to reach, so it draws both newer ice climbers and people just coming to watch. Expect company on good weekends. Conditions depend entirely on the freeze, so check the current ice report before heading up.

nm_south_cliffband.blurb: South Cliffband is a section of Cochiti Mesa in the Jemez area of New Mexico, known for harder lines than most of the mesa. There are fifteen routes, mostly bolted with two trad lines, and the grades stack up in the 5.11s and 5.12s with a few 5.10s and a single 5.9. Expect thin slabs, cracks and some steep overhanging sections, and a handful of lines that can also be top-roped. The cliff turns a bit more toward the west than its neighbours, so it holds shade longer into the day. Reach the base from the downclimb by heading southeast, or rappel from the rim to some of the routes.

ns_planet_of_the_apes.blurb: A cluster of boulders on the shore of Digby Neck, facing the Bay of Fundy, in the Sandy Cove area. There are eighteen problems, all bouldering, and the field is known as the densest concentration of boulders in the region. Most lines fall between V0 and V4, with a handful of V1 and V2 problems to warm up on and a single problem near V6 for the strong. The stone is clean, grippy basalt. Getting in means travelling along the shoreline over rocks rather than on a trail, so wear sturdy shoes. Expect a quiet, uncrowded place; many more problems exist here than are listed.

ok_04_headwall.blurb: The Headwall is a granite wall on Quartz Mountain in the Wichita range of southwest Oklahoma, the third of the mountain's big formations and visible from the parking area. There are twelve routes: mostly trad, four bolted lines and one aid route. The grades lean hard. A handful of easy-to-moderate leads at 5.6 and 5.8 give way to a few 5.10s and 5.11s, and 5.12 is the most common level, topped by a 5.13. Expect bold, friction-dependent face climbing on this mountain, and note that the sun reaches most of the rock for much of the day, which makes cooler months the comfortable choice.

or_great_arch_the.blurb: The Great Arch is the main sport wall on Wolf Rock, the biggest freestanding rock in Oregon, tucked in the Cascade foothills east of Eugene in the Willamette Valley region. There are nineteen routes, almost all of them bolted single pitches with a pair of trad lines mixed in. The grades lean hard toward the 5.10s, with a good handful of 5.11s, a few 5.9s, and just a couple of easier lines in the 5.7 range. That makes it better suited to climbers who already lead the middle grades than to true beginners. Expect a remote forest crag feel rather than a roadside crowd scene.

tn_mystery_groove_boulder.blurb: One of the boulders in the Front Area of Stone Fort, the well known bouldering field in the woods beside a golf course near Chattanooga. It lies in the first cluster of stones you meet on the way down from the parking area. There are about ten problems, running from very easy up to V6, with a few in the low-to-moderate range and the boulder's best known line around V4. Several faces and a back side offer different angles, so a group of mixed ability can all find something. Expect a busy, popular part of the field.

wv_shadow_boxer_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering spot in the Good Block Area of Tilted Tree, the busiest climbing zone in Coopers Rock State Forest near Morgantown. There are ten problems, and the spread is wide: several easy lines from V0 to V2, a V3, then a big jump to the namesake V6 classic and a V10 test piece at the top end. That mix gives beginners something to warm up on while strong boulderers have a long-standing goal. Expect company on weekends, since the zone draws crowds, and bring pads.

wv_4_fire_and_ice_buttress.blurb: A buttress in the Kaymoor section of the New River Gorge, placed midway between the two trails that lead down to the Kaymoor cliffs. There are ten routes, mostly trad (seven) with three bolted lines. Nothing here is easy: four routes sit in the 5.10 range, three in 5.11, two in 5.12 and one in 5.13, so it is a place for climbers already comfortable leading the 5.10s. Rock is sandstone.

ca_loaf_the_2.blurb: A single boulder group in the Buttermilks, the famous boulder-strewn hillside west of Bishop in the eastern Sierra. There are ten problems. Most fall between V0 and V4, with a couple of much harder lines at V7 and V8, so there is something for a warm-up and something for a project. The face looks west, which brings afternoon sun. The wider hillside is known for flat, sandy landings and roadside access along Buttermilk Road, and you can start from the parking area below the main boulders.

ca_condome_2.blurb: Condome is a granite dome in the Shaver Lake area of the western Sierra, set between the lake and the northern end of Bald Mountain. The formation has two tiers with most of the routes on the lower one, and the climbing is mostly bolted slab. There are ten routes, seven sport and three trad, from 5.8 to about 5.10, with the greatest number around 5.10. Some gear can be handy, particularly for building anchors if you carry on to the top of the lower tier. It is a quiet corner for moderate slab, and the walk from the road is short.

nj_m_the_great_arch.blurb: A section of Mt. Tammany in the Delaware Water Gap, just beyond the double-overhang stretch of the cliff, which is its steepest and most dramatic part. There are ten climbs, nine of them traditional and one aid line, in a range running from 5.3 up to the low 5.11s, with most of the weight in the 5.6 to 5.8 band. Many of the best-known lines are two pitches long. Gear is placed from the ground up in the area's traditional style, and the quartzite takes protection well. Descending can be involved, with a rappel that hangs free under a big roof, so bring two ropes and care.

ny_gravity_rules_area.blurb: Gravity Rules Area is a section of Antlion Cliff, a backcountry band of rock in the Gunks south of Millbrook. It begins at the top of the stone steps and carries on leftward. There are ten trad routes, spanning the mid 5.x grades up to the 5.12 range, with a cluster around 5.10. Trees give the wall partial shade. The cliff is still being cleaned, and lower Millbrook-style rock can be sandy and loose, so place gear carefully. Expect a hike of a bit over a mile with a steady climb to reach the cliff.

pa_little_fluffy_clouds_area.blurb: Little Fluffy Clouds Area is a small cluster of boulder problems along the Caves Trail on Haycock Mountain, in the Nockamixon part of southeastern Pennsylvania. There are about a dozen problems, and the range is wide for such a compact spot: several easy problems at V0 to V2, a solid middle group around V4 to V5, and a few hard lines above that, topped by one very difficult V9. The namesake traverse is the best-known problem and a regular objective for visiting boulderers. Expect a wooded trailside setting rather than a roadside crag, and bring pads.

ak_eklutna_canyon_2.blurb: A popular winter ice and mixed area north of Anchorage, with climbs on both the north and south walls of the canyon cut by the Eklutna River. There are about two dozen lines, mostly mixed in the lower to middle M grades, with a smaller set of water-ice routes from WI2 to WI4. Expect a long, easy walk down to the river and then upstream.

va_a_v_p_boulder.blurb: This is the main block of a small boulder cluster in the Grayson Highlands of southwest Virginia, set in forest at roughly 3,800 feet. There are about two dozen problems, and the bulk of them fall between V2 and V5, with a short run of much harder lines reaching V9. Expect steep, powerful moves on small holds, and good landings. The boulders sit very close to the road, so this is an easy place to squeeze in a short session or to start a day before heading to the other blocks nearby.

wy_1_blooming_rose.blurb: Blooming Rose is a sport wall in the OK Corral section of the high-plateau Wild Iris area outside Lander, at roughly 8,900 feet. It shares its cliff line with Claim Jumper and Saddle Tramp, and it is a good stop for climbers who want plenty of mid-grade pulling. There are about twenty-two climbs, nearly all bolted, with a single boulder problem. Grades start around 5.7 and run up to the low 5.13s, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with 5.11 the most common. Expect other parties on the wall, and reach it by following any of the trails that branch off the main dirt road.

co_us_highway_550.blurb: A string of frozen waterfalls along the road that climbs south from Ouray toward Red Mountain Pass. There are twenty-five ice lines, nearly all of them WI4, with a few WI5s and one WI3, so this is mostly an intermediate-to-advanced venue. A few mixed pitches turn up as well. Many lines are visible from the roadside and the walk to the base is generally short, which makes for quick days, though several are multi-pitch and some sit under big snow bowls. Avalanche hazard after heavy snowfall is a real consideration, and ice quality changes a lot from one winter to the next.

wa_beetle_bailey_slab.blurb: A granite slab in the Lower Lump area at Index, in the Skykomish Valley, reached with a short walk from town. About 38 climbs, split between bolted sport lines and trad, with a few going multi-pitch. Grades start around 5.6 and run to 5.12, but most sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it suits intermediate and stronger climbers; the lower grades are better found on neighbouring walls. Large maples shade the base, which makes it pleasant on hot days, though the slab can stay wet after rain. The upper part of the slab sits on land bought for public ownership by climbing groups.
